claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a well-characterized hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure has been documented using high-resolution electron microscopy and orientation imaging.
A regression-based machine-learning model trained on microstructural descriptors can predict Young's modulus of HfNbTiVAl10.
A regression-based machine-learning model trained on microstructural descriptors can predict yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10.
A regression-based machine-learning model trained on microstructural descriptors can predict fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-boundary density mediates the macroscopic mechanical response of the hierarchical heterostructure.
Second-phase volume fraction mediates the macroscopic mechanical response of the hierarchical heterostructure.
Inter-phase connectivity mediates the macroscopic mechanical response of the hierarchical heterostructure.
Statistical learning of relationships between microstructural descriptors and macroscopic responses can provide a surrogate for full-field simulations.
The machine-learning model will reduce prediction error by approximately 30% relative to established simulations.
The machine-learning model will reduce computation time by approximately 50% relative to established simulations.
Halving computation time will enable near-real-time mechanical-property assessments.
Predictive performance may fail outside the strain-rate or loading regime represented during calibration.
Predictive performance may fail if the selected descriptors omit mechanically important heterogeneities.
Unrepresented phase transformations may cause the model to fail.
Preliminary modeling and imaging evidence supports the feasibility of the proposed machine-learning approach.
